oom.title: Out of memory (OutOfMemory)
oom.fix: Increase allocated RAM in the profile Java settings. Close other apps and heavy shaders.

wrongJava.title: Wrong Java version
wrongJava.fix: Newer Minecraft versions need Java 17/21. Pick a matching runtime in Java settings or install one automatically.
wrongJava.fixNeed: Java {{java}} or newer is required. Select it in the profile's Java settings or install it automatically.
wrongJava.fixTooNew: Java {{java}} is too new for this loader version. Pick an older runtime in the profile's Java settings (usually 8 or 17).

mixinConflict.title: Mixin / injection conflict
mixinConflict.fix: Disable recently added mods one by one. Two mods patching the same code is a common cause.

modIncompatible.title: Mod loading failure
modIncompatible.fix: Check mod versions for your Minecraft and loader (Fabric/Forge/Quilt). Remove duplicate .jar files.

missingDependency.title: Missing mod dependency
missingDependency.fix: Install required libraries (e.g. Fabric API, Architectury, Kotlin for Forge) matching the mod version.

versionMismatch.title: Minecraft version mismatch
versionMismatch.fix: Download the mod built for this pack’s Minecraft version. Mods for other versions usually won’t start.

corruptJar.title: Corrupt JAR file
corruptJar.fix: Reinstall the broken mod/library. Avoid downloading mods from untrusted sources.

openglGlfw.title: Graphics error (OpenGL/GLFW)
openglGlfw.fix: Update GPU drivers, try windowed/fullscreen, and disable overlays (Discord, GeForce Experience).

authFailed.title: Authentication failed
authFailed.fix: Sign in again via Microsoft/Ely.by on the Accounts tab. Online servers need a valid session.

exitCode.title: Game exited with an error
exitCode.fix: Check ERROR lines above and crash-reports in the pack folder. Raising RAM or removing the last mod often helps.

diskSpace.title: Not enough disk space
diskSpace.fix: Free space on the drive that holds the game folder and launcher cache.

accessDenied.title: File access denied
accessDenied.fix: Run the launcher with write access to the game folder. Close antivirus or apps locking files.

nativeCrash.title: Native JVM crash
nativeCrash.fix: Update drivers, switch Java runtime, and temporarily disable mods with native libs (Sodium/Iris, etc.).
nativeCrash.fixDriver: The crash happened inside the graphics driver ({{module}}). Update the GPU driver from the vendor's site and turn off overlays and shaders.
nativeCrash.fixJvm: The Java VM itself crashed ({{module}}). Switch the Java runtime in the profile settings and check the allocated memory.

fabricLoader.title: Fabric Loader / API issue
fabricLoader.fix: Update Fabric Loader and Fabric API to versions compatible with your Minecraft version.

forgeVersion.title: Forge version issue
forgeVersion.fix: Install the recommended Forge version for this pack, or update mods to match your Forge.

jvmStart.title: Java failed to start
jvmStart.fix: Usually more memory is allocated than available (or a 32-bit Java is used). Lower RAM in the profile's Java settings or install a 64-bit Java.

badJvmArgs.title: Invalid JVM arguments
badJvmArgs.fix: Java doesn't recognize one of the launch options. Remove it from the extra JVM arguments in the profile settings.

dependencyVersion.title: Wrong dependency version
dependencyVersion.fix: The required mod is installed, but in the wrong version. Update it (or the dependent mod) to a compatible version.

duplicateMods.title: Duplicate mods
duplicateMods.fix: The same mod is installed more than once. Keep a single version — the pack's Conflicts tab can do it.

apiMismatch.title: Mod built for another version
apiMismatch.fix: A mod calls a class or method that doesn't exist. Usually the mod or its library is for a different Minecraft version. Update the mod and its dependencies.

crashReport.title: Game crashed (crash report)
crashReport.fix: The cause from the report is shown below. If mods are listed, start with them.

worldCorruption.title: World corruption
worldCorruption.fix: Part of the world data can't be read. Restore the world from a backup or delete the damaged regions.

shaderCrash.title: Shader error
shaderCrash.fix: The shader pack failed to compile. Update Iris/Oculus and the shader pack, or turn shaders off.

source.label: Download source
source.hint: Where game files, libraries and loaders come from. In automatic mode the launcher switches to a mirror on its own when the official servers stop responding.

tickingEntity.title: The game crashed while ticking an object in the world
tickingEntity.fix: A broken entity or block (often from a mod) takes the world down when it loads. Update or disable the mod that owns it; for vanilla objects, restoring the affected chunk from a backup helps.

serverWatchdog.title: The integrated server hung
serverWatchdog.fix: A single game tick took too long and the watchdog stopped the game. Heavy world-generation mods or huge farms are the usual cause. Give the game more memory and check recently added mods.

stackOverflow.title: Stack overflow
stackOverflow.fix: Code ended up calling itself endlessly. Most often two mods keep calling each other. Disable recently added mods one at a time.

missingRegistries.title: The world contains blocks or items from removed mods
missingRegistries.fix: The world was saved with mods that are not installed now. Bring those mods back, or confirm removing their content when you join the world (make a backup first).

linuxXrandr.title: xrandr not found
linuxXrandr.fix: Older Minecraft versions on Linux need the xrandr tool. Install x11-xserver-utils (Debian/Ubuntu) or xorg-xrandr (Arch).

optifineConflict.title: OptiFine conflicts with your mods
optifineConflict.fix: OptiFine changes game code in a way Mixin mods cannot work with. Disable it and use Sodium + Iris (Fabric/Quilt) or Embeddium + Oculus (Forge/NeoForge).
